question: What type of germ is Salmonella?
explanation: You got it! Salmonella is a single-celled bacterium that loves to multiply quickly when conditions are just right. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h1)

question: How do viruses usually spread through food compared to bacteria?

options.A: Viruses require high temperatures to activate inside raw meat products.
options.B: Viruses use food as a vehicle to spread from person to person without multiplying in the food.
options.C: Viruses only grow on surfaces with high sugar content.
options.D: Viruses are naturally occurring plant toxins found in unwashed vegetables.

explanation: Spot on! While bacteria can multiply inside food, viruses just hitch a ride on the food to travel from one person to another. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h1)

question: When washing your hands, what is the minimum time you should scrub with soap?
explanation: Great job! Scrubbing for at least 20 seconds is the golden rule to properly lift and wash away germs from your skin. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h2)

question: A kitchen worker has a small healing cut on their finger. What should they do before handling food?

options.A: Cover it with a waterproof bandage and wear a clean glove
options.B: Apply palm oil to the cut to create a natural barrier against germs
options.C: Stay home for the entire week until the cut is fully closed
options.D: Wash the finger with cold water and continue working normally

explanation: Spot on! Open cuts carry lots of bacteria like Staphylococcus, so always seal them up with a waterproof cover and a glove. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h2)

question: What temperature range is known as the 'danger zone' where food safety is at risk?
explanation: Correct! Bad bacteria multiply super fast when food hangs out in this 5°C to 60°C danger zone. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h3)

question: Where is the best place to store raw poultry inside a refrigerator to avoid contamination?
explanation: You got it! Always put raw meat on the lowest shelf so any accidental drips stay far away from ready-to-eat foods. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h3)

question: What does 'cross-contamination' mean in a kitchen setting?

options.A: The transfer of harmful pathogens from one surface or food to another
options.B: The chemical reaction that occurs when mixing two different spices
options.C: The freezing of fresh vegetables at incorrect freezer temperatures
options.D: The natural spoilage of food caused by exposure to direct sunlight

explanation: Spot on! Cross-contamination happens when germs travel from a dirty source (like raw meat) over to safe food (like a fresh salad). [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h4)

question: A cook slices raw beef and immediately uses the same unwashed knife to cut fresh tomatoes. What just happened?
explanation: Correct! Using the same knife without washing it transfers bacteria directly from the raw meat into the fresh veggies. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h4)

question: Which of these is an UNSAFE way to thaw frozen meat?

options.A: Using the defrost setting on a microwave oven
options.B: Submerging it securely in cold running tap water
options.C: Leaving it on the kitchen counter at room temperature
options.D: Thawing it slowly inside the refrigerator compartment

explanation: You nailed it! Leaving meat on the counter lets the outside warm up into the danger zone where bacteria love to multiply. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h5)

question: Why should a large, hot pot of soup be split into shallow containers before putting it in the fridge?

options.A: To allow the food to cool down quickly and escape the danger zone
options.B: To stop the liquid from changing color during refrigeration
options.C: To make the soup easier to season with spices later on
options.D: To prevent the refrigerator door from staying open too long

explanation: Great thinking! Shallow pans help hot food cool down fast so it doesn't linger in the warm danger zone. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h5)

question: What is the main difference between cleaning and sanitizing a kitchen surface?

options.A: Cleaning uses chemical agents, while sanitizing only uses plain water.
options.B: Cleaning is done after food prep, while sanitizing is done before food prep.
options.C: Cleaning kills all bacteria, while sanitizing only removes visible grease.
options.D: Cleaning removes dirt and food, while sanitizing reduces microorganisms to safe levels.

explanation: Spot on! Cleaning washes away visible dirt and food, while sanitizing goes after the invisible germs using heat or chemicals. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h6)

question: What is the most effective way to keep pests out of a kitchen?

options.A: Leaving all windows open overnight to allow fresh air circulation
options.B: Sweeping the floor once a week after closing business hours
options.C: Keeping food stored off the floor in sealed containers and sealing entry gaps
options.D: Spraying strong insecticides in the dining area every morning

explanation: Correct! If you block their entry points and hide their food source in tight containers, pests won't bother showing up. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T009#GNS227_U3_T009_h6)
